one_variable_ablation.removed_variable: negative 15-minute open-interest change at the first retest

failure_structure: The accepted-break and exact-first-retest geometry is not one economic mechanism. Contracting OI represents liquidation/reduction, while non-contracting or expanding OI represents fresh inventory. Removing the OI gate reverses the sign of performance across the two weeks rather than producing a stable improvement, so the same entry scenario cannot be applied across both inventory states.
largest_performance_factor: Inventory mechanism at retest, interacting with the surrounding auction state. Treating OI as a global include/exclude threshold caused false generalization.
valid_components: The parent state begins with an actually accepted causal external-pool break rather than a rolling-return sign.
The broken pool itself is the only eligible first retest level; unrelated historical pivots are excluded.
Outside acceptance and reclaim are completed-data states with aligned flow, return and basis.
The non-climactic relation prevents a larger second impact event from being mislabeled as orderly resumption.
next_use: Retain accepted-break and exact-first-retest detection as a context primitive. Future systems must route contracting-OI liquidation retests and expanding-OI inventory retests as separate complete scenarios with independent parent-state requirements; do not combine them with OR logic.
